audit_notes: Model: steady diffusion of mobile functional species (cleaved zwitterionic segments or free oil) through the topcoat, xi = depth/depletion_depth, xi=0 at the wetted surface (perfect sink, c=0), xi=1 at the reservoir front (c = free mobile concentration). Volumetric source S = k*c_bound from linker cleavage. Analytical: c = (S L^2/2D) xi(1-xi) + c_free xi, surface loss flux J = (D/L) dc/dxi(0) = S L/2 + D c_free/L. Design (oil-free, tethered): S = 3e-10*100 = 3e-8 kg/(m^3 s), J = 3e-8*1.5e-4/2 = 2.25e-12 kg/(m^2 s) = 0.07 g/(m^2 yr); over 5 years 0.36 g/m^2, i.e. 2.4 % of the 15 g/m^2 tethered inventory. Baseline: conventional foul-release coating with 4.5 wt% free silicone oil (c_free = 45 kg/m^3, no tethered species, k = 0): J = 1e-15*45/1.5e-4 = 3.0e-10 kg/(m^2 s) = 9.5 g/(m^2 yr), which would exhaust the 6.75 g/m^2 oil inventory within a year (consistent with reports that oil-containing foul-release coatings lose their oil and performance within 1-3 years; the pseudo-steady model overestimates the late-stage flux because the front recedes). Expected gain ~99 % lower loss rate of functional material (degradation_rate). Caveats: (1) same diffusivity used for both species (conservative for oil, which diffuses faster); (2) not every conventional foul-release coating contains free oil; against an oil-free PDMS baseline the loss-rate comparison is meaningless because such a coating has no hydration function to lose; (3) the loss rate of material is only a proxy for the loss of the anti-slime function, which may fail earlier by conditioning films or surface reconstruction, not modelled. Dimensionless: ratio of cleavage source to diffusive flux S L^2/(D c_free) = 3e-8*2.25e-8/(1e-15*45) = 0.015; linker half-life ln2/k = 73 years. Stress check: no structural load; hydrophilic segments at 10 wt% cause swelling of a few percent, acceptable. Simulation coefficient: design loss flux 2.25e-12 kg/(m^2 s) (informational).
